My name is not important, but I will tell you how I farm my maize here in Mangochi. This year I was lucky to get the coupon from the government, so I bought one bag of NPK and one bag of urea — it is not enough for the whole plot but I put it close to the maize plants. I plant my maize together with pigeon peas, because pigeon peas help the soil and also give us food later in the dry season. I keep some chickens and a few goats, so I carry their manure to the plot before the rains. I cannot afford hybrid seed every year, but this year with the coupon I got some improved seed from ADMARC. The rains come from November, so I do not irrigate — I wait for the sky. My wife and my older children help me, but for the first weeding I sometimes pay a neighbour small ganyu if the weeds are too much.
